background: Bendigo and Adelaide Bank is Australia's largest regional bank, funded mainly by retail deposits raised through a community-branch model and lending mainly on residential mortgages and to farms and small businesses.
synthesis: All three main agencies rate the bank A-, all on a stable outlook, the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 21 Nov 2025. Capital is the weak spot, with CET1 of 11.3% in the bottom quarter of Australian banks, while liquidity is strong, with LCR of 140% in the top quarter and NSFR of 115% above the peer median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods to 30 Jun 2026. The newest flagged item, on 18 Sep 2026, is job cuts concentrated in Adelaide; earlier items cover a return to profit for the year and an AML-related capital charge.
